No product-recognition accuracy claim'; w6-recognition-scale.md, Tiny validation evidence: 'Real watcher reports idle'; What integration / a person supplies: 'Real hardware/shelf data ... remain unmeasured.'","evidence_class":"real-shelf-validation","supported":"yes","decision_informed":"Present the shelf box as an experimental client, not validated autonomous recognition; prioritize real capture before claiming replenishment autonomy.","caveat":"This is missing evidence, not evidence that the approach cannot work; it also says nothing about the gateway's lookup, quote, order, approval, or audit capabilities."},{"claim":"Kimi repeatedly named catalogue products for a tested non-product shelf crop, and list permutations did not eliminate that behavior.","evidence":"r3-full-first-summary.md, SYNTHETIC false-product bias: steady-01-crop Kimi base 6/15 = 0.400 (0.198-0.642), L-permutations 15/50 = 0.300 (0.191-0.438); synthetic-control Kimi 0/3 base and 0/9 permutations.","evidence_class":"synthetic","supported":"yes","decision_informed":"Do not use candidate-conditioned Kimi output alone to trigger shortage or order proposals; require rejection/veto and human approval.","caveat":"Repeated frames and answers are dependent, the negatives are concentrated on hard crops, and the intervals do not support a general false-positive rate or a significant base-versus-permutation comparison."},{"claim":"The Kimi payload diagnostic supports image delivery and candidate-list conditioning as a cause of changed descriptions in the tested cases.","evidence":"kimi-payload-20261114/README.md, 11-request table and Findings 1-3: controls and unconditioned crop descriptions match pixels; the same crop becomes a yoghurt tub or milk carton with candidates.","evidence_class":"synthetic","supported":"yes","decision_informed":"Test candidate-free description and independent verification rather than spending more effort only on list shuffling.","caveat":"Eleven diagnostic requests on a few crops establish a mechanism in those cases, not its frequency across products, sessions, or prompts."},{"claim":"Qwen rejected every negative in the current partial bias suite, but positive recognition evidence is insufficient.","evidence":"w6-recognition-scale.md, Final verification / first full results: qwen2.5-vl-7b items 355, named_product 0, named_milk 0, parse_failures 0, infra_failures 0; conditioning-full-first-summary.md has only isolated 1/1 positive rows.","evidence_class":"synthetic","supported":"yes","decision_informed":"Treat Qwen as a candidate for a conservative rejection pipeline, not as the selected production recognizer.","caveat":"An always-unknown policy would also score perfectly on these negatives; the suite does not establish real product recall, and the full batch was still running."},{"claim":"Rendered-label successes demonstrate only OCR-like synthetic positive handling.","evidence":"kimi-payload-20261114/README.md, final two table rows: two rendered labels mapped to the correct candidates; vlm-models/evidence/first-results.md, synthetic/reference-strategy: qwen-7b text-only 1/1 card match.","evidence_class":"synthetic","supported":"partly","decision_informed":"Include balanced positives and negatives in the next evaluation; do not demo these card results as package recognition.","caveat":"Rendered names and GTIN cards are not real packaging, and no visible-identifier barcode/OCR shelf inputs were supplied."},{"claim":"Embedding and RGB-template methods have different augmentation-consistency failure modes.","evidence":"r3-full-first-summary.md, SYNTHETIC augmented recorded views: DINOv2 brightness same-view 12/12 at thresholds 0.5-0.85 but blur falls 6/12 to 2/12 and rotation/occlusion reach 0/12 at 0.95; template-rgb blur remains 45/45 through 0.85 while brightness falls 35/45 at 0.5 to 0/45 at 0.95.","evidence_class":"synthetic","supported":"yes","decision_informed":"Use augmentation tests to design a conservative veto and lighting/capture requirements, not to claim product identity accuracy.","caveat":"These are small augmented-view consistency tests with n=12 or n=45 per cell; the 0.85 threshold and 0.03 margin are explicitly provisional and not calibrated on held-out sessions."},{"claim":"Qwen cloud inference is operational on A100, with only preliminary latency, memory, and cost observations.","evidence":"vlm-models.md, Current detached work: A100 load 14.814 s and observed post-load memory 17,211 MiB; first-results.md, infrastructure/cold-runtime and synthetic/latency-cost: warm observations about 0.41-0.99 s in the shown synthetic rows.","evidence_class":"measured-infrastructure","supported":"partly","decision_informed":"A cloud-hosted recognition service is feasible to prototype; keep UNO Q edge-performance claims and production cost commitments out of the pitch.","caveat":"Latency tables contain one or two queries, memory is sampled after loading rather than a final inference peak, and estimated costs exclude cold start, idle, builds, storage, egress, and persistence overhead."},{"claim":"The recognition harnesses reportedly implement resumable experiments, human-validation gates, and session-separated real evaluation, but integration verification is still required.","evidence":"w6-recognition-scale.md, Delivered and Final verification: scale_app.py/real_eval.py features and self-reported 213 passed, 6 skipped; vlm-models.md, opening and Git handoff limitation: 17 local tests passed but no commit was created.","evidence_class":"code-claim","supported":"partly","decision_informed":"Coordinator should inspect, commit, and rerun the harness before relying on it for the demo or production-path story.","caveat":"These are writer-reported code and test claims; Writer C remains an uncommitted worktree/patch, and passing plumbing tests does not validate recognition or ordering behavior."},{"claim":"The documents do not contain final full-batch model comparisons or final costs.","evidence":"w6-recognition-scale.md, Final verification JSON: 'First downloaded subset only; detached work continues' and full_app_metered_cost_snapshot 0.49735918; vlm-models.md: 1,989 synthetic items planned per successfully smoke-tested model, but only first results were confirmed and $2.43098379 was a lagging partial snapshot.","evidence_class":"measured-infrastructure","supported":"yes","decision_informed":"Do not select models or quote total experiment spend from these snapshots; collect durable outputs and final billing after jobs stop.","caveat":"Detached jobs may have progressed after the documents were written, so current Volume state must be inspected rather than assuming these are still the latest totals."}],"unsupported_or_overstated":["'The shelf client recognizes Valio products accurately' or any real-shelf accuracy, UNO Q latency, or deployed-behavior claim.","'Qwen is production-safe, accurate, or the best model' based on zero named products in the negative suite.","'Kimi has a general 30-40% false-positive rate' or 'permutations significantly improve/worsen it'; keep current supported runtime, unresolved models, and final-cost status.","Keep the real-data schema as a short upload/validation checklist rather than repeating watcher and label-contract details across handoffs."],"negative_results":["No human-validated reference/evaluation recordings exist, so all real tables are idle and no real product accuracy or UNO Q measurement exists.","Kimi's false product naming was not caused by an obviously missing image in the diagnostic, and candidate-list permutations left substantial observed false naming.","Qwen's perfect negative rejection is not accompanied by enough positive evidence to distinguish useful recognition from blanket rejection.","DINOv2 consistency degraded sharply under blur, occlusion, and rotation; RGB templates degraded severely under brightness changes and stricter thresholds.","In the tiny baseline check, CLIP retained only 1/3 blurred identities at 0.85 and the actual two-photo detector returned uncertain on all six views; these are smoke findings, not final comparisons.","The DeepSeek probe returned HTTP 403 with no generated tokens.","Gemma E4B stopped before inference because its audio submodel rejected SDPA; Gemma 12B and Nemotron had no confirmed successful load or predictions.","No real visible-identifier barcode/OCR inputs were supplied, and the proposed recognition threshold/margin remain uncalibrated.","Full outputs and final billing are incomplete, no monetary cap was imposed, and Writer C's implementation was not committed."],"open_question_worth_a_run":["Run a session-disjoint UNO Q shelf holdout: record at least three independent capture sessions covering every demo SKU, non-catalogue look-alikes, empty slots, occlusion, moved products, and lighting variation; human-validate labels, train/reference only on designated sessions, freeze thresholds before evaluation, and report per-SKU correct acceptance, false product acceptance, unknown rate, false shortage decisions, and end-to-end UNO Q-to-service latency.","On that same frozen holdout, run a paired Kimi/Qwen prompt ablation using identical frames: candidate-conditioned matching, candidate-free describe-then-match, and independent per-candidate verification, with randomized candidate order. Select a policy only using jointly reported positive recall and negative rejection, with session-level intervals and measured cloud latency/cost, rather than negative rejection alone."]}
